title.title: Hypersymplectic 4-manifolds deform to hyperkähler
title.subtitle: Claim: a normalized hypersymplectic triple deforms to a hyperkähler one, so the 4-manifold is K3 or $T^4$

plain: Three interlocking structures that almost fit perfectly can always be bent until they fit exactly

lines.note: span positive definite at every point
the corollary experts will test first

beats.text: Three symplectic forms that look like a hyperkähler triple, but need not be parallel
Donaldson conjectured in 2006 that they can always be deformed to the real thing
Compact hyperkähler 4-manifolds are K3 or tori, which pins down the topology

steps: Deform the three forms step by step, keeping their classes fixed
Current estimates from the taming proof keep the path under control
The path ends at a true hyperkähler triple

achievement.label: Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture (2006)
achievement.context: Corollary: a closed 4-manifold with a hypersymplectic structure is diffeomorphic to K3 or $T^4$
achievement.note: Reuses the Lean-checked estimates of family 342; the deformation is paper-only

verify.ourCheck: We read the claim; we did not check the deformation argument

voice.text: Three symplectic forms that look hyperkähler, but need not be parallel at all.
Deform them with classes fixed; estimates from the taming proof keep it under control.
Claimed: it always reaches a hyperkähler triple.

sources.quote: Donaldson ('Two-forms on four-manifolds and elliptic equations', 2006) conjectured the deformation
every hypersymplectic triple normalized by integral omega_i ^ omega_j = delta_ij deforms through hypersymplectic triples, fixing all three cohomology classes, to a hyperkaehler triple
A hypersymplectic structure is a triple of closed 2-forms whose span is positive definite at every point, like a hyperkähler triple without parallelism.
a closed 4-manifold with a hypersymplectic structure is diffeomorphic to K3 or $T^4$. That corollary is where I would expect experts to push first.
72 pages; builds on the current estimates of family 342 (which is formalized) but the prescribed-class deformation arguments are not formalized.
